errors.english: By these words, the lord of men
errors.why: With 'ma bkur' from the previous side this is 'by that dishonour' (Skt. vimānena), i.e. the Nāgas' contempt, not 'these words'.

note: Faithful verse rendering of the bilingual jātaka side; only the cause of the king's dejection is misidentified at the boundary.

errors.english: That [note: the ultimate nature] is not of the same category as those [note: ordinary perceptions]. If you ask who possesses those perceptions:
errors.why: The root says 'that is not [knowable as] reality — by whom? by all who do not see the supreme'; the 'category' reading and both notes are wrong.

fix.find: That [note: the ultimate nature] is not of the same category as those [note: ordinary perceptions]. If you ask who possesses those perceptions:
fix.replace: That is not known as reality. If you ask by whom:

errors.english: regarding the meaning of reality which possesses equanimity [note: original: "upeksha"], characterized as being free from definitions: those who are the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones,
errors.why: 'Indifferent to the object of reality' qualifies the Buddhas, who treat the reality-object (free of characteristics) with indifference; reality does not 'possess equanimity'.

fix.find: regarding the meaning of reality which possesses equanimity [note: original: "upeksha"], characterized as being free from definitions: those who are the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones,
fix.replace: those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who are indifferent [note: upekṣā] to the object of reality, which is free from characteristics,

errors.english: [note: a steady, unblinking, and panoramic way of looking]
errors.why: The elephant's look (gajanimīlikā) is feigned non-seeing, seeing yet acting as if one did not, as the sentence itself goes on to say.

fix.find: [note: a steady, unblinking, and panoramic way of looking]
fix.replace: [note: gajanimīlikā, the elephant's feigned not-seeing: seeing but acting as if one does not see]

note: Generally follows the commentary, but the root verse 'not knowable as reality, by whom?' and 'indifferent to the reality-object' are misparsed and the elephant-gaze note is wrong.
Accurate rendering of the Nyāyabindu commentary on the three modes and the unestablished reason, with correct technical terms.

errors.why: This completes the previous side's sentence: sons were also born to the other thirty-four queens (the 'youths' that follow), not Moon.

errors.english: even a slight trace of lowliness is prevented by their very birth
errors.why: The verse argues qualities outweigh lineage: the lowliness of birth is cancelled (by qualities), not prevented by birth.

errors.english: Possessing virtuous qualities and noble intelligence, he became a highly respected and grave figure.
errors.why: This opens a general gnomic verse on qualities versus birth; it is turned into a prose statement about Moon.

errors.english: marked with the name of the regional governor
errors.why: dum bu 'dzin pa looks like the proper name of the former lord (who later speaks of being robbed of his lordship), rendered as a title.

note: Narrative prose is mostly right, but the boundary sentence and the inserted verses on birth versus merit are misread.

errors.english: bypasses the customs process without attachment
errors.why: ma chags here means the customs duty was not incurred, not 'without attachment'.

errors.english: If the carrier is positioned on land belonging to the boundary but has no specific purpose, there is no downfall.
errors.why: It means: where (with spells or medicines) no carrier standing on land inside the boundary is needed, there is no offence.

note: Sound rendering of the Vinaya discussion of customs evasion through the air; two clauses are misconstrued.

errors.english: has not been rendered suitable for consumption by a youth
errors.why: khye'u kha 'thon pa appears to be a third object (an emerged sprout) that has not been made allowable; 'kha 'thon' is dropped and a 'youth' agent introduced.

note: Accurate account of the bhūtagrāma pāyattika and the five seed-types; one phrase in the definition of the offence is doubtful.
A careful rendering of the argument about the word 'certainty' and why seeing and not-seeing cannot establish pervasion.

errors.why: The double negative says the opponent holds that certainty of the whole arising from memory and recognition is by no means uncertain.

note: Good rendering of the debate over the whole (avayavin), except that the opponent's key claim is negated.
Faithful word-by-word gloss of the tigress episode in the Jātakamālā commentary.

errors.english: used because of the desire to express clarity
errors.why: gsal ba is vyakti, the individual instances; the plural is used to refer to the individuals.

fix.find: used because of the desire to express clarity
fix.replace: used because the intention is to refer to the individual instances (vyakti)

errors.english: the very mental consciousness that forms the connection is the mind
errors.why: sems dpa' here is sattva (the being), and mtshams sbyor is rebirth-linking (pratisandhi).

fix.find: the very mental consciousness that forms the connection is the mind
fix.replace: the very mental consciousness that links rebirth (pratisandhi) is the being (sattva)

errors.english: If the support makes the state of destruction occur
errors.why: The point is the support causing the persistence (sthiti) of the perishable thing, not causing destruction.

errors.english: because that which causes destruction does not remain, as it remains of its own accord
errors.why: It says: a cause of persistence is pointless, because when no destroyer is present the thing persists by itself.

note: The refutation of the support (āśraya) as a cause of persistence is muddled, and two technical terms are mistranslated.
